planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring or early fall into humus-rich, evenly moist soil in part to full shade; a North American native, it tolerates deer pressure and resists most pests and disease.

directions: Set out divisions in spring into moist, organically rich soil beneath open or dappled tree canopy, watering regularly until the arching clump is established. Noble Native carries creamy white variegation along narrow blue-green leaves, forming a low, fountain-like mound that works well edging shaded paths or woodland borders. It is evergreen in milder zones and spreads slowly, so little division is needed beyond occasional clump refreshing. Being native and deer resistant, it fits naturalized shade plantings with minimal upkeep.

planting.note: Set container plants in spring into well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; unlike woodland bleeding hearts, this alpine type dislikes soggy winter soil.

directions: Plant in a sunny to lightly shaded bed with sharp drainage, since this alpine-type bleeding heart rots in wet winter soil despite tolerating more sun than its woodland relatives. Pixie Hearts holds finely dissected, blue-green foliage and blushing pink flowers from late spring well into fall, outlasting the bloom window of old-fashioned Dicentra spectabilis. Deadheading is unnecessary since it reblooms steadily on its own, and the compact habit suits border fronts and containers. Deer tend to leave it alone, and it draws bees and butterflies through its long season.

planting.note: Divide and plant dormant crowns in spring or early fall into moist, humus-rich soil with pH 5.5-7.5, in part to full shade.

directions: Plant divisions in a shaded woodland-style bed with consistently moist, organically rich soil, setting crowns at their original depth. Frog in My Throat shows an unusual reversed variegation pattern, pairing dark green margins with flecked creamy-white centers that differs leaf to leaf across the clump. Near-white flowers appear on scapes in early summer, but the foliage display is the main draw. Mulch annually to retain moisture and protect the shallow root system through summer heat.

planting.note: Give this giant hosta generous room when dividing and planting in spring or fall, in moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade.

directions: Site this giant hosta where its mature 6-7 foot spread has room to fill in, in consistently moist, organically rich soil beneath open shade. Leaves emerge chartreuse and mature to a smooth, deeply veined golden yellow, forming a dramatic focal clump unusually fast for a hosta this size. Pale lavender flowers appear on tall scapes in early to midsummer above the foliage mound. Keep soil evenly moist while the clump establishes, then allow slight drying between waterings in later seasons to avoid crown rot.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade; morning sun only, since afternoon sun scorches hosta foliage.

directions: Tuck this miniature hosta into a shaded container, rock garden pocket, or edging row where its small scale won't be overwhelmed by larger neighbors. Mouseketeer resembles the popular 'Blue Mouse Ears' but runs larger overall, with broad yellow leaf centers, fine green flecking, and variegation that extends down the petiole toward the base. Purple flowers rise on short 8-10 inch scapes in early summer. Keep soil evenly moist and limit direct sun to gentle morning light to preserve the leaf coloring through the season.

planting.note: Set out container plants in early spring or fall into consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade; shallow roots need reliable moisture and a protective snow or mulch cover over winter in cold zones.

directions: Plant in a shaded bed or container with rich, continuously moist soil, since this primrose's shallow roots dry out quickly without consistent water. Berry Darling opens fully double, solid burgundy-red blooms that are sterile, which lets the plant push out flower after flower across early, mid, and late spring rather than setting seed and stopping. Foliage stays compact and bright green between bloom flushes. In cold climates, mulch or ensure snow cover over winter to protect the crown from hard freezes.

planting.note: Set out container plants in early spring or fall into consistently moist soil in part to full shade; protect from hard freezes with snow cover or mulch where winters are harsh. One of three Bouquet Perfect primroses Walters Gardens released for 2026, alongside 'Watercolour Blue'.

directions: Grow Rosalina in a shaded border or container where its tidy, rounded habit and large, clean-edged blooms can be seen up close. Flowers are bright pink with a crisp white picotee edge, and because the blossoms are sterile the plant keeps producing new flowers through early, mid, and late spring instead of going to seed. Keep soil consistently moist, since the shallow root system suffers quickly in dry spells. Bees visit readily, and plants benefit from snow or mulch cover over winter in colder zones.
